TOPIA instances, cut from the shipped model

Source: R/topia-build.R
build_topia.Rd

The dataset ships ONE model: twelve provinces, hourly, 51 objects. This cuts smaller cases from it – one province, one zone, a sample across zones – in a single call, resolving as it goes the things that are tedious and error-prone to do by hand.

Usage

build_topia(
  regions = NULL,
  preset = NULL,
  layout = "honeycomb",
  level = "province",
  calendar = "d365_h24",
  horizon = "BY2025_50_by10",
  techs = NULL,
  modules = NULL,
  clusters = TRUE,
  demand = NULL,
  weather = NULL,
  levers = TRUE,
  as = c("kit", "model", "repository"),
  boundary_prices = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

regions

province codes, zone codes, the nation code, or a count for the first n in canonical order. NULL keeps all twelve.

preset

one of "full", "island" (R01, no wire and no domestic fuel) or "zone" (Z3, carrying the nuclear station and the reservoir). A preset expands to the arguments below and reports what it chose.

layout

"squares", "honeycomb" (the default, and the one the shipped model carries), "island" or "continent".

level

the geoframe the model's own regions are. Only "province" is built so far.

calendar

a calendar name or object. It must be a sample of the model's own – its timeslices a subset of d365_h24's – which d365_h24_1dpm (301) and d365_h24_1dps (101) are. Anything else is refused, naming the slices that do not match.

horizon

"BY2025_50_by10", "BY2025", or a horizon object.

techs

which technologies to keep, or to drop with a leading - (c("-EBIO", "-H2ELC")). Two keywords are derived from the objects rather than listed: "vre" is a technology declaring a weather series, "thermal" one that burns its input. Keeps and drops cannot be mixed.

modules

which of the article's nine sub-repositories to keep, or to drop with a leading -: commodities, supply, weather, generators, storage, hydrogen, transmission, fuel_trade, demand. modules = "-hydrogen" strips in one word the chain the article declares across three sections.

clusters

not built yet.

weather, demand

the name of a shipped dataset ("sample", "simulated") or a data.frame shaped like the matching element of topia_profiles() – so the output of one is the input of the other. The frames are written into the shipped objects, which keeps each series' name, units and timeframe. A weather frame must cover every (cluster, region) pair the object's roster declares; a demand frame carrying load is a relative shape and is scaled to the annual energy the shipped object holds, one carrying demand is taken as given.

levers

TRUE for all four, FALSE for none, or names.

as

"kit" (the named list the dataset itself uses, so the two are interchangeable), "model" (a ready newModel() with the geoscale set), or "repository".

boundary_prices

passed to subset_model_regions() to price the corridors a subset cuts.

quiet

suppress the one-line report of what was built.

Value

A kit (named list), a model, or a repository.

Details

build_topia() authors nothing. Every object it returns was declared in TOPIA I: building the model, which generates the shipped data files; this selects from them. A technology TOPIA does not declare cannot be asked for, and new processes are added to the article rather than here.

With every argument at its default the result is topia$modules$electricity unchanged, which is what tests/testthat/test-topia-build.R pins.

regions takes codes at any geoframe. A zone code expands to the provinces beneath it, so a request never cuts a zone in half by accident – which matters because COA and GAS balance at the zone, and a subset that splits one is refused by subset_model_regions() rather than averaged.

Selecting processes pulls a dependency closure behind it: drop every coal burner and COA, SUP_COA, IMP_COA and both coal corridors go too, because nothing is left to use them. A storage and a corridor are not counted as consumers or producers while deciding this – one time-shifts and the other moves, so counting them lets a commodity keep itself alive after its last real user is gone. CO2 is reachable only as an emission declared on COA and GAS, and is kept on that basis. A lever naming a process that is gone goes with it, since it would otherwise reference what the model does not declare.

A cheaper calendar re-keys the series and the demand curve onto it, and the annual energy is held fixed: a sample is a cheaper view of the same year, not a smaller year, and two cases are only comparable if the demand they must meet is the same. Only a sample of the model calendar is accepted. The measured wind and solar grades exist on d365_h24 alone, so a calendar with timeslice names of its own – s4_h24, whose series are a simulated stand-in with no grades at all – would leave every clustered technology with no weather row and running unbounded.

The two levers that carry a spatial shape are narrowed with the model: GREEN_H2, whose for.each names every province, and CO2_CAP, whose cap is a per-province allowance times the province count and so is rescaled by the count kept. CT_CO2 and EARLY_RET have no province dimension.

layout chooses which of the four pictures the model is drawn on. The corridor network is the SAME on all four – fourteen corridors frozen in data-raw/topia_links.R, not derived from any one layout – so a layout changes the map and nothing the model solves.

See also

topia for the dataset, subset_model_regions() and aggregate_model_regions() for the reduction verbs this sits beside.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# the shipped model, unchanged
identical(build_topia(), topia$modules$electricity)

# one zone, ready to interpolate
mod <- build_topia("Z3", as = "model")

# the island, by name
kit <- build_topia(preset = "island")
} # }
